t: Built c. 2600 BCE over about 26 years as the tomb of the pharaoh Khufu, it stood as the world’s tallest human-made structure for more than 3,700 years.
Its chambers carry no inscriptions but the painted names of work-gangs, yet those names, the Diary of Merer and the cemeteries of Khufu’s family and officials tie it firmly to his reign.
Ancient Greek writers believed slaves built it; finds at the nearby workers’ camps suggest that thousands of conscript labourers did.
dyk: Rolls of papyrus found at Wadi al-Jarf in 2013, the Diary of Merer, record a supervisor’s deliveries of white limestone from Tura to the pyramid in the 27th year of Khufu’s reign, naming it dozens of times by its original name, Akhet Khufu.
ev: The pyramid is built as the tomb of Khufu over a period of about 26 years
Herodotus attributes the pyramid to Cheops, the Greek form of Khufu’s name, but places his reign after the Ramesside period
The Abbasid caliph al-Ma’mun is said to have tunnelled into the pyramid and found the ascending passage and its chambers
Amid earthquakes in northern Egypt, casing stones stripped from the pyramid are said to have been carted away for use in nearby Cairo
Cyriacus of Ancona visits Giza and refutes the medieval belief that the pyramids were the granaries of Joseph
Howard Vyse opens the four upper relieving chambers, whose painted work-gang names spell out Khufu’s names
Kamal el-Mallakh finds a sealed boat pit at the south foot of the pyramid holding the dismantled Khufu ship
The ScanPyramids project detects a large cavity above the Grand Gallery, the “Big Void”, whose purpose is unknown

f.made: Built for Khufu (Cheops), pharaoh of the Fourth Dynasty of the Old Kingdom; his vizier Hemiunu is believed by some to have been its architect; finds at the nearby workers’ camps suggest it was raised by thousands of conscript labourers organised in named work-gangs
f.form: A pyramid of an estimated 2.3 million blocks, mostly local limestone, once cased in white limestone from Tura, with granite from Aswan in the King’s Chamber; originally 146.6 m high, now 138.5 m, each side of the base about 230.3 m; three main chambers, the Grand Gallery and five relieving chambers inside
f.where: On the Giza plateau in Giza, Egypt, part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site “Memphis and its Necropolis”; the Khufu ship from its boat pit is in the Grand Egyptian Museum, two objects from the Queen’s Chamber shafts are in the British Museum and a cedar plank from them at the University of Aberdeen
f.known: the oldest of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World; the world’s tallest human-made structure for more than 3,700 years; the precision of its base and its alignment to the cardinal directions; the Grand Gallery and the King’s Chamber; the work-gang graffiti naming Khufu; the Diary of Merer; the Khufu ship
